persona: FSBO-curious skeptic homeowner in Cherry Hill, NJ — leaning toward selling without an agent to save the ~5% commission, willing to use Steven's free tools/data but resistant to giving contact info until an agent proves they're worth the fee.
device: desktop (static dist/**/*.html inspected; mobile layout not separately rendered)
journey_notes: Entered on /home-value/cherry-hill/ (seller intent). The lead form ('See What Your Cherry Hill Home Could Sell For': Name, Address, Town, Zip, Email, Phone) sits ABOVE the actual market data. As a skeptic I'm asked for my home address + phone before the page gives me anything. Reflex: scroll past the form, not fill it.

Below the form the real value finally appears: Cherry Hill median $368,500, down 11.2% YoY, 31 days on market, 34% sell above list, labeled 'balanced market.' This is genuinely useful and free — exactly what I came for. I take it and feel no obligation.

'Why Work With a Local Agent?' section = three generic cards (Real Data / Local Knowledge / Maximized Value). It ASSERTS an agent adds value but never addresses my actual objection: is that value worth 5%? No FSBO comparison, no data, no proof. It reads as a brochure, not an argument that respects my intelligence.

Went to /tools/proceeds-calculator — the standout. Honest, specific NJ breakdown: commission, Realty Transfer Fee, the NJ 'exit tax' (GIT 2% withholding), title, ~$1,500 attorney. This earns real trust and tells me the site isn't hiding costs. BUT the commission slider min is 1%, max 7% — I literally cannot set it to 0% to model selling FSBO with no agent. The one tool a commission-skeptic most wants to run against 'do it myself' quietly assumes I'll hire someone.

/tools/should-i-sell-now and /tools/home-value-estimator both deliver free location data with 'no signup required' — good, low-friction, respect-building. But every tool result terminates in the SAME lead form + 'request a free CMA / book a consultation.' The estimator even openly says 'the estimator gives you a range, a CMA from Steven gives you the exact number' — useful framing, but it's the only next step offered.

Searched the whole 357-page site for any FSBO / 'sell it yourself' / 'is an agent worth it' content: ZERO. There is no page, paragraph, or stat that honestly engages the for-sale-by-owner decision (e.g., FSBO-sells-for-less data, what an agent actually does for the fee, net-after-commission vs net-FSBO). The single biggest question on my mind is unaddressed across the entire site.

Checked /about for proof the agent is good: 'data analyst background,' 'data first, education over pressure' — likable positioning and on-brand for me. But NO track record: no homes-sold count, no years of experience, no testimonials, no reviews, no sale-price-vs-list results. Nothing lets me verify the expertise I'm being asked to pay 5% for.

Credibility ding a skeptic notices: homepage county cards all say "Seller's Market" while the same page's summary says 'Seller's Markets 0 (0%) / Balanced Markets 97 (100%).' A self-contradiction on the front page makes me trust the 'data-driven' claim a little less.

Convert-or-bounce: I extracted everything I wanted (market snapshot + a clear net-proceeds estimate) WITHOUT giving any contact info. At the proceeds-calculator CTA I'm asked for name+address+email+phone to 'maximize my proceeds,' but I've seen no proof an agent nets me more than FSBO and no rebuttal to my commission objection. I bounce — tools bookmarked, contact info kept.

friction.point: No FSBO / 'why an agent vs selling yourself' content anywhere on the site
friction.note: The persona's core decision is never engaged. Missing the one honest argument (agent-net vs FSBO-net, what the fee buys) that could actually earn the call from a skeptic.

friction.point: Proceeds-calculator commission slider locked to 1%–7% (cannot model 0%/FSBO)
friction.note: The most FSBO-relevant tool silently assumes an agent. A '0% / For Sale By Owner' setting that then shows the offsetting risks (FSBO typically sells for less, no MLS exposure, my own time) would be both honest AND the strongest pro-agent argument on the site.

friction.point: Lead form placed above the value on home-value town pages
friction.note: Asking for home address + phone before delivering any data triggers a skeptic's funnel-radar and gets scrolled past.

friction.point: Zero social proof / track record (no sold count, testimonials, reviews, years)
friction.note: Persona is explicitly judging whether the agent is worth the fee; the site gives nothing to verify competence. TestimonialCard exists but is empty per project rules — real proof is needed.

friction.point: 'Why Work With a Local Agent' = generic asserted benefits, no evidence
friction.note: Reads as brochure copy; doesn't out-argue a DIY-leaning reader.

friction.point: Every tool/page funnels to the same single CTA (CMA / consultation form)
friction.note: No lower-commitment middle step (e.g., emailed FSBO checklist, 'agent vs FSBO net' PDF) for someone not ready to hand over a phone number.

friction.point: Homepage market-type contradiction (counties 'Seller's Market' vs summary '100% Balanced')
friction.note: Undermines the data-credibility positioning a skeptic is specifically testing.

biggest_blocker: The site never engages the FSBO-vs-agent decision at all — no honest commission-worth-it argument and no track record/social proof — so a skeptic gets full free value from the (genuinely good) tools and data with nothing that justifies handing over contact info or paying 5%.
score_justification: Tools and proceeds breakdown build real trust, but with no FSBO rebuttal, no proof of results, and a contact-gated funnel, the skeptic takes the value and leaves.
